baseline_models.focus_anchor: `ma lahum bihi min ilm wa-la li-aba'ihim` and `in yaquluna illa kadhiban`
baseline_models.mechanism: The claim lacks both direct disclosure and ancestral transmission; nevertheless a saying has hardened into inherited belief, so the final falsehood verdict audits provenance as well as content.

activation_trace.role: Disclosure of an object is explicitly absent, removing direct epistemic warrant.
Fatherhood and upbringing supply the intergenerational channel whose knowledge is also denied.
Saying as belief or doctrine lets the utterance function as a transmitted position, not only a sentence.
Contradiction of truth names the result of maintaining that unwarranted position.

changed_reading.before: The ayah says that an assertion is false.
changed_reading.after: The ayah performs a provenance audit: neither the current speakers nor the ancestral channel can supply knowledge for a belief they still voice.

baseline_models.mechanism: The syntax stages the word as a weighty object crossing a bodily threshold. Its production is vivid, but its only demonstrated route is from mouth to outside rather than from knowledge to speech.

activation_trace.role: What has grown great becomes difficult to carry, giving the utterance burdensome force.
An intelligible word that can expand into a whole saying supplies the object being carried outward.
Passage from an interior station to the outside gives the utterance its directional motion.
An opening that serves as an outlet turns the mouths into the claim's visible point of origin.
Speech brought out in articulated form completes the conversion of internal production into public assertion.

changed_reading.before: A very serious word is spoken.
changed_reading.after: The word is staged as a heavy object whose only demonstrated route is outward through a bodily opening; vivid oral production contrasts with the absent route from knowledge.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening supplies a counter-trajectory: a composed communication is delivered downward, remains free of semantic bend, and stands upright; the condemned word instead travels outward from human mouths with no disclosed support.

activation_trace.role: Movement from an interior station to the outside gives the human claim its ejected trajectory.
The mouth as outlet fixes the human trajectory at a bodily source.
Causing something to descend and reach its recipient supplies the opposed trajectory of delivered communication.
Letters joined into an ordered written object give the delivered speech composed form.
Semantic deviation is explicitly negated, making unwarped meaning part of the contrast.
Straightness and balanced standing sharpen the delivered book's stable orientation.

structural_cues: 18:1-2 place a delivered book that has no semantic bend and is upright before the warning in 18:4-5.
18:2 word 6 (`ل د ن`, branchless) places the warning 'from with Him' and supports the source contrast without a fabricated branch citation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies delivery, written composition, negated bend, uprightness, and bodily exit; I infer a directional contrast between received straight speech and self-originating mouth-output. A live alternative is that this geometry is rhetorical framing rather than a claim that oral form itself is defective.

changed_reading.before: The phrase merely locates a false utterance in its speakers' mouths.
changed_reading.after: Against delivered, composed, straight communication, the ayah marks the claim as self-ejected oral production whose source and shape lack external warrant.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context resolves the claim as assigning acquired offspring to God. Human speakers project the grammar of lineage upward while neither they nor their own fathers know it; the later demand for compelling, manifest warrant classifies that projection as fabrication.

activation_trace.role: Human parenthood and nurture make the denied ancestral knowledge pointedly relevant to a claim about divine offspring.
Absent disclosure removes any known basis for transferring human lineage categories to God.
Taking as acquisition specifies the asserted divine relation as something adopted or obtained.
Offspring issuing within a lineage supplies the concrete content projected onto God.
A proof with compelling force defines the level of warrant the lineage claim fails to bring.
Manifest disclosure requires the alleged proof to emerge clearly rather than remain inherited assertion.
Deliberate invention of falsehood identifies the mechanism that fills the evidentiary vacancy.
The repeated contradiction of truth seals the later proof-demand to the focus ayah's verdict.

structural_cues: 18:4 immediately precedes the focus and resolves `bihi` as the saying that God has taken offspring.
18:15 repeats `ittakhadhu`, demands a clear authority, and closes with the same `kadhiban`.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies acquisition, offspring, denied knowledge, a proof-demand, and fabrication; I infer an ironic recoil in which humans generalize their own lineage grammar to God without warrant. The live alternative is that the fathers simply broaden the denial across generations without activating that irony.

changed_reading.before: The ayah rejects an unsupported theological claim.
changed_reading.after: It exposes a specific projection mechanism: speakers universalize human acquisition and descent into divine genealogy, then ancestral repetition substitutes for the clear authority they cannot produce.

context_deltas.mechanism: The cave sequence develops an evidentiary trail from remaining marks, through inscription, to an account that follows the trace and conforms to reality. That chain gives true report a recoverable path, unlike the focus claim whose only stated provenance is the mouth.

activation_trace.role: Knowledge as disclosure is missing, creating the focus ayah's evidentiary vacancy.
A distinguishing mark that guides toward its object contributes a secondary branch echo: the claim has no guiding marker.
The mouth as outlet remains the only explicit trail that can be followed back from the false claim.
A remaining mark that indicates what preceded it begins the context's recoverable evidence chain.
An inscribed line in a record gives the chain a durable documentary station.
Following one trace after another supplies a method for producing the account rather than merely voicing it.
Stable correspondence with reality gives the traced account its truth condition.

structural_cues: The sequence advances from `atharihim` in 18:6, through `al-raqim` in 18:9, to `naqussu ... bil-haqq` in 18:13.
The focus construction names mouths but no intermediate source, witness, sign, or record.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mark, inscription, trace-following, and reality-conformity; I infer that accountable speech has a recoverable trail while the focus claim has mouth-only provenance. The mark branch of `ilm` is a resonance, not a replacement gloss; the simpler alternative is only a contrast between knowledge and ignorance.

changed_reading.before: The speakers happen not to possess knowledge.
changed_reading.after: Their claim is structurally untraceable: true report can be followed through marks and record toward reality, whereas this word can be followed only back to mouths.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later dialogue distinguishes provisional speech that retreats to superior knowledge from repeated claims that cast guesses into hidden matters. The focus therefore criticizes uncalibrated assertion: lack of knowledge becomes falsehood when conjecture is voiced as settled belief.

activation_trace.role: The explicit absence of disclosure establishes the knowledge limit that speech must respect.
A saying functioning as supposition exposes the possible transition from estimate to overconfident assertion.
Contradiction of truth marks the endpoint when unsupported supposition hardens into doctrine.
Successive sayings move from a rough temporal estimate to an explicit yielding of the matter to better knowledge.
Superior disclosure assigned to their Lord terminates rather than disguises the speakers' uncertainty.
Repeated sayings circulating among people turn uncertain enumeration into competing public reports.
Guessing speech aimed into what is unseen gives the failed epistemic method a projectile image.
What is screened from sight defines the domain into which the unsupported sayings are cast.
The repeated knowledge terms relocate certainty with the Lord and the few who actually know.
The closing assignment of better knowledge to God fixes the proper endpoint of unresolved speech.
The hidden domain belongs to God, setting a jurisdictional boundary around human assertion.

structural_cues: 18:19 explicitly moves from a rough duration estimate to `rabbukum a'lam`.
18:22 triples `they will say`, labels guesses as casting into the unseen, and limits dispute; 18:26 closes with `God knows best`.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies estimate, deference, repeated enumeration, hiddenness, and superior knowledge; I infer a norm of calibrated speech rather than blanket silence. A live alternative is that 18:5 is categorically false while 18:19 and 18:22 only model posture, so uncertain statements are not false merely because they are uncertain.

changed_reading.before: Having no knowledge means that the speakers should simply remain silent.
changed_reading.after: The ayah targets speech that conceals its uncertainty: an estimate may be voiced and then yielded, but conjecture cast into the unseen becomes falsehood when performed as settled knowledge.

context_deltas.mechanism: The command about tomorrow extends epistemic discipline from claims about hidden divine relations to claims about one's own future agency. A mouth must not convert intention into settled reality; divine will and remembered qualification keep the saying contingent.

activation_trace.role: The missing disclosure anchors the danger of speaking beyond what is presently knowable.
Articulated public speech supplies the focus construction later governed in the command about tomorrow.
The explicit prohibition regulates bringing a future claim out in speech.
The next day supplies the not-yet-realized domain that the unqualified saying prematurely settles.
Will attached to the thing inserts divine contingency into the projected action.
Restoring what slipped from awareness supplies the corrective that requalifies speech.
Loss from remembrance explains how an overconfident future utterance can omit its epistemic limit.

structural_cues: 18:23's prohibition is syntactically completed by the exception and remembrance command in 18:24.
The pair repeats the focus root `ق و ل` while shifting from a claim about God to a claim about the speaker's own future act.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies saying, tomorrow, divine will, remembrance, and forgetting; I infer that the focus critique opens into an ethic of contingent future speech. A live alternative is that 18:23-24 is a local command about planning and does not directly revise the offspring claim.

changed_reading.before: The focus ayah condemns one false doctrine about God.
changed_reading.after: It also seeds a wider discipline of the mouth: desire and intention must not be grammatically promoted into settled future fact without remembered contingency.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it combines form-distant bodily branches of `kalimah` and `takhruju` with the adjacent grief sequence. It remains anchored in the focus word, its outward motion, its burden, and 18:6's threatened self-destruction; downstream prose should present it only as an embodied material analogy, never as a replacement lexical gloss for `kalimah`.

activation_trace.role: The bodily injury branch gives the word an exploratory capacity to wound rather than merely inform.
A sore emerging from the body turns outward speech into an eruptive lesion image.
Difficult weight gives the eruptive word a burden borne by those it reaches.
Self-destruction under grief supplies an adjacent image of bodily damage following rejected speech.
Torment over loss gives the receiving side of the speech-wound its affective force.

changed_reading.before: The false utterance is intellectually and morally offensive.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the word exits like an eruptive wound and helps produce a counter-wound of grief in the hearer.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates rare non-endurance and deceptive-garment branches of `kadhiban` through the adornment-to-barrenness sequence. It remains anchored in the focus falsehood and in 18:7-8's test, beautification, and stripped ground; downstream prose should qualify it as a material analogy for exposure over time, not as the ordinary lexical meaning of `kadhib`.

activation_trace.role: A garment that misrepresents its own condition lets falsehood operate as an attractive but deceptive surface.
Expected continuity that suddenly fails gives the deceptive surface a temporal limit.
Making a thing appear beautiful supplies the surface attraction that can conceal its actual state.
Testing that makes a condition show itself supplies the exposure mechanism.
The alternate mapped root also frames trial as disclosure of the real condition, preserving the packet's split mapping.
Ground stripped of growth supplies the terminal image after ornament has been removed.

changed_reading.before: The lie simply fails a truth test.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it is a beautified surface whose apparent continuity survives only until testing strips it and exposes a barren substrate.

strongest_changes: The immediate context turns the generic lie into human genealogy projected onto God without compelling, clear warrant.
The opening contrasts delivered, composed, straight speech with a word whose only demonstrated origin is a human mouth.
The cave sequence distinguishes traceable account and calibrated uncertainty from conjecture cast into the unseen.
18:23-24 extends the critique into future speech that must remain contingent on divine will and remembrance.
summary.what_was_special: The packet made source geometry, evidentiary trails, and speech calibration converge on one focus: the problem is not merely an incorrect proposition but a mouth-generated claim that outruns provenance, evidence, and epistemic jurisdiction. Bodily-wound and deceptive-surface branches remain live only as contained material analogies.
remaining_uncertainties: The contrast between descending book and exiting word may be deliberate spatial rhetoric or a reader-supplied geometry.
The mark sense of `ilm` and wound sense of `kalim` are branch echoes, not replacements for ordinary syntax.
18:22 models conjectural method, but one enumerated count may still be correct; the critique concerns warrant and posture, not automatic falsity of every estimate.
The future-speech extension is coherent but less tightly tied to the specific offspring claim than the 18:4/15 chain.
